# Release Notes: v1.0.10

> This file is the source of truth for the GitHub Release body.
> The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release-android.yml`)
> copies this file's contents as the Release body via `body_path`.

## Android

- **"Tracking" streak renamed "Log streak"** — the tile counts consecutive days
  with logged activity, so "Tracking: 0 days" next to a multi-day goal streak
  read like a data error. The value and its calculation are unchanged; the web
  client uses the same label

## Web (already live on Hosting)

These shipped through Firebase Hosting and need no app update; they are listed
here so this release records everything since v1.0.9.

- **Google sign-in fixed for returning visitors** — the service worker routed
  cross-origin Google/Firebase requests through itself, where the CSP blocked
  the sign-in script (`apis.google.com`). All service-worker routes are now
  same-origin only; a PWA regression check asserts cross-origin scripts bypass
  the worker (#131)
- **Tighter Content Security Policy** — reCAPTCHA-era origins
  (`https://www.google.com`, `https://*.google.com` frames) removed from both
  hosting configs (#130)
- **Charts** — round y-axis ticks that are never clipped (a 292-unit month now
  reads 0/100/200/300/400), and the last 7-day label reads "TODAY" instead of
  "NOW", which looked like the month "NOV" (#132)
- **Readability** — semibold text renders at its real weight, a drop in usage
  shows in green rather than the red accent, text is at least 11 px, the
  session log is part of the page instead of a nested scroll box, Delete
  account is an outline button, and Save buttons are solid (#132, #134)

## CI

- Emulator teardown in the instrumentation job is bounded (30 s `adb`, 20 s
  grace before `SIGKILL`), so a stuck shutdown can no longer fail a run whose
  tests passed (#133)
- `ui-test-manifest` pinned to the version Gradle actually resolves (1.12.1)

## Compatibility

- Firestore Security Rules: comment-only changes since v1.0.9 (#130); no rule
  logic changed
- No Cloud Functions are deployed and no Blaze plan is required; the app runs
  entirely on the Firebase Spark plan (Auth + Firestore + Hosting)
- No change to Authentication configuration, billing, or production data
